## What had to be provisioned, and what had to be worked around
The nested linked worktree arrives with no node_modules, so the verification
toolchain does not exist until it is installed. The command run at the delivered
tip was:
$ pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts
No lockfile work and no package.json edit were needed. Two workarounds, both
disclosed rather than hidden:
  * '--ignore-scripts' skips postinstall native builds (better-sqlite3). The
    suites below do not load a native binding, so they run and pass regardless.
    No engine source was changed to make that true.
  * vitest is invoked as './node_modules/.bin/vitest run <file>' from inside the
    package. The package's own 'test' script expands to 'vitest run
    --reporter=dot', which takes no file argument position this card needs.
Toolchain as installed: vitest/4.1.10 linux-x64 node-v26.10.0; node v26.10.0.

## Every test file in the package's src tree, on the new base
$ (cd packages/pi-claude-cli && NO_COLOR=1 ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src --reporter=verbose)
exit code: 0
counters :  Test Files  16 passed (16)|      Tests  387 passed (387)|
skipped entries in that run: 0
The whole-tree run is included because 'the suite I picked is green' is the
claim AC2b is sceptical of. Here the whole src tree is green on the new base, so
nothing this card reports later is hiding a pre-existing failure in this package.
Per-test bodies are omitted from this file on purpose: the file argument that
would narrow the run is exactly the shape AC2b rules out, so the run is broad and
its counters line is what is quoted, not a filtered subset of its rows.

So this card is NOT green on that gate and does not claim to be: it exits non-zero
repo-wide. raw/red-green.txt measures the same gate with this line's module
